MCCQE Part 1 Overview

The Medical Council of Canada Qualifying Examination (MCCQE) Part 1 is a one-day, computer-based examination that assesses critical medical knowledge and clinical decision-making at the level expected of a medical student completing their degree in Canada. Passing the MCCQE Part 1 is required to obtain the Licentiate of the Medical Council of Canada (LMCC) and is a prerequisite for entry into a Canadian residency program for international medical graduates.

Following the 2025 reform, the exam consists entirely of multiple-choice questions - the Clinical Decision-Making (CDM) component has been permanently removed. The exam is structured around two broad categories: Dimensions of Care (covering the spectrum of medical care) and Physician Activities (reflecting a physician's scope of practice). Content is mapped to the CanMEDS framework.

MCCQE Part 1 Details

FormatComputer-based MCQ exam (CDM removed in 2025)
Questions230 multiple-choice questions in 2 sections of 115 items
Duration6.5 hours total (160 min per section + optional 45 min break)
BlueprintCanMEDS roles, Dimensions of Care, Physician Activities
DeliveryPrometric test centres or remote proctoring (70+ countries)
Pass mark226 (revised scale 100-400)
Sessions4 per year (Jan-Feb, Apr-May, Aug-Sep, Oct-Nov)
AttemptsUp to 4 attempts (1-year wait after third attempt)
Official source: mcc.ca ↗

Eligibility & Requirements

  • A medical degree from a school listed in the World Directory of Medical Schools (WDOMS) with Canada sponsor note.
  • PhysiciansApply.ca account with source-verified medical degree and final transcripts (~CAD $335 setup).
  • Application submitted up to 15 months before graduation; 12-month eligibility window from approval.
  • Payment of MCC examination fees (~CAD $1,330 total inclusive of all assessment costs).
  • For IMGs: also required to complete the NAC OSCE for residency eligibility.
